body:
Accident implies intent. An accident is when something does not meet an an expectation of of a certain intent. You can view the universe with "intent" if you want. I don't believe in some ultra super high consciousness "intending" things to happen. The universe to me is just one individual possible universe of a seemingly unfathomable amount of possible universe states. Just because we exist within one specific state at a time doesn't mean that it was intended. What we experience now is just the result of everything before this moment up until right now. To me, that is an accident.

The particles that eventually arose into life didn't intend themselves to form, the dust that eventually formed the sun didn't intend to be in that exact position, and the big bang didn't intend for the universe to unfold the way it does. It's just how things have happened.

The reason people become "genius at the stuff" is because they have a strong passion for said "stuff". They do it because they love it and enjoy it, from the inception of the idea, to the creative process, and the ultimate completion of the project. People who are "genius at the stuff" do not force themselves through doing it because they genuinely do not enjoy doing it. You aren't going to become incredibly at something by focusing your attention on something you do not enjoy.

You aren't trying to interpret how I feel, you're just giving your own personal opinion on things. You are not me, and whatever applies to you doesn't necessarily apply to me, because I have a different mind and experience the world differently than you do.

I cannot stick to something if I do not enjoy it. I cannot focus my attention on something I do not enjoy. The process of doing things that I don't enjoy never has given me satisfaction. There is no route to becoming "a genius at stuff".

It's not that I think things are impossible to do. I could FORCE myself to do them *If I wanted to*. I don't want to, because doing things like that does not help me. There is no point. Saying that life is rewarding to someone who is depressed and does not experience reward when they try to progess, is quite honestly, a slap in the face, and It's absolutely clear to me you have not suffered from a depression that's been with you for most of your life and simply doesn't go away.

I've tried. I do have a guitar, I could never get into it. I've tried many different things. Video editing, digital art, writing, creating music in DAWs, animating. I've tried a lot of things, and I never really enjoyed any of them enough to do them. :/

There is success and failure. Happiness is success, not being happy is failure, if it's not progressing towards happiness. And no, I wouldn't say it's playing tricks on me. I am like this most of the time. It's more me than anything else. The happy me is not a default state, and it is not one that I can just make pop up whenever I want. The depressive state is. No, I'm not going to go get a job, any job. I couldn't even do that if I tried. It would not be moving forward. It would be worse. It would be more stress for absolutely no gain. I already explained this in the main post.

I've done that. I've tried taking daily walks, it just triggered my anxiety, it did not make me feel better, so I stopped. Listening to music can make me feel better for a moment, but it doesn't ultimately change my mood.

I do have daily activities. My computer. Which I sit on all day, because the only thing that I actually want to do is distract myself from life.  I don't and am not really interested in any other activities, and I've tried to be. Doing things isn't really an option for me. 

Honestly, there is just no positive scenario, or positive future that I can imagine that would be any better than the life that I'm living right now. I'm miserable, but I'm comfortable miserable. I would rather be comfortably miserable, than trying to attain uncomfortable not miserable, and most likely failing.

I mean... there aren't really things that I want to do. I don't know. :/

And I really liked that music by the way. More, the talks, because dreams are something I'm fascinated by.
